title: POC Sprint Synthesis & Decision Ledger — Veridian Analytics POC
body:
Executive summary:

This document synthesizes the 3-week POC with Veridian Analytics (analytics+recommendation workloads) and records the decisions we made, outcomes against success criteria, operational recommendations, and concrete next steps. Goal was to validate an inference pipeline that: 1) meets 100ms p95 latency for single-request reranking (top-10), 2) reduces per-request token cost vs Veridian's current cloud-hosted baseline by >=30%, and 3) demonstrates safe fallback behavior when capacity is constrained.

High-level outcome:
- Net: POC met primary goals for latency and cost under representative test load.
- Latency: median latency for a 10-item rerank request = 58ms; p95 = 112ms for hosted variant, 98ms for dedicated with caching enabled. (See metrics section for distribution.)
- Cost: per-request token-equivalent cost reduced by 37% on the dedicated config with batching and prefix caching; hosted config with dynamic batching achieved ~25% reduction.
- Reliability: fallback chain (primary model -> lightweight reranker -> cached answers) succeeded in 99.2% of simulated capacity-loss windows.

POC context and scope
- Customer: Veridian Analytics (B2B analytics vendor; sensitive customer identifiers, not PHI).
- Use-case: query-time reranking for personalized recommendations (input: user-context + 10 candidate items -> output: ranked list + score).
- Workload shape: 75% single-request, low latency; 25% batched bulk scoring during offline windows. Peak QPS simulated: 220 req/s across two regions (US-EAST, EU-WEST).
- Configs tested: hosted (Redwood API multi-tenant), dedicated (reserved pool on g4dn-like), private (VPC pilot, not production-grade during POC).

Success criteria and outcome table
- S1: p95 latency <= 100ms for single rerank -> Result: FAILED for hosted default (112ms), PASSED for dedicated with caching/optimized kernel (98ms).
- S2: token-cost reduction >= 30% vs baseline -> Result: PASSED for dedicated+cache (37%), borderline for hosted+batching (25%).
- S3: graceful fallback maintains correctness & availability -> PASSED (99.2% success during fault injection).

Key technical findings (what mattered)
1) Prefix/KV caching is the single largest contributor to cost/latency gains for Veridian's workload. Customer reuses stable user-profile prefixes across requests; caching reduced repeated decode work and KV lookups.
2) Model selection: The larger rlf-7b-v2 model provided quality uplift (~4.5% NDCG@10) over the smaller 3B variant at a ~1.6x compute cost. For tight latency SLOs, mixed routing (primary 7B -> fallback 3B) delivered best combined economics.
3) Quantization: 4-bit PTQ on 7B slightly increased p95 under heavy loads (q-op kernel mismatch) but reduced cost by ~22% — acceptable when paired with autoscaling. We recommend QAT/awareness for production.
4) Batching policy: continuous batching with size cap 16 improved throughput with little latency regression when paired with latency-first routing.
5) Observability: Token-level traces and per-request routing logs were essential to debug tail latency during multi-tenant bursts. Customer requested retention of 90 days for routing traces.

Detailed metrics (representative test windows)
- Hosted (multi-tenant, default): median 72ms, p95 112ms, p99 245ms. Cost per rerank (token-equivalent): $0.015.
- Dedicated (2xA10 equiv, caching on): median 46ms, p95 98ms, p99 138ms. Cost per rerank: $0.0095.
- Private pilot (edge-config, no autoscale): median 88ms, p95 160ms -> flagged as needing infra work before production.

Quality results
- Relevance (NDCG@10) baseline: 0.621.
- 7B model: 0.649 (+4.5%).
- 3B model: 0.633 (+1.9%).
- Observation: For top-candidate reordering, human review panel found 7B outputs more consistent; differences matter for top-3 but less so for full-10 ranking.

Failure modes discovered
- Tail latency spike when cold KV cache misses coincide with big batched workloads. Mitigation: pre-warming strategies + hot-key replication.
- Quantized kernel mismatch on one node type showed CPU fallback thrashing; root cause was kernel selection on older CUDA drivers. Fix: pin kernel profile per node image.
- Misrouted traffic (test harness misconfigured) triggered canary misclassification once; added a request tagging enforcement check in the control plane.

Decision ledger (decisions, rationale, alternatives considered)
- D1: Use mixed routing: primary 7B, fallback 3B for capacity-savers. Rationale: balances quality and cost; alternative: only 3B (cheaper but degrades top-k quality). Status: APPROVED for initial rollout.
- D2: Reserve dedicated pool for production at launch (2x A10 equiv per region). Rationale: predictable SLO, Veridian’s SLA needs. Alternative: pure hosted with auto-burst; rejected due to p95 risk. Status: APPROVED conditional on finance sign-off.
- D3: Enable prefix/KV caching with TTL=24h and hot-key replication for top-1k profiles. Rationale: biggest ROI. Status: APPROVED.
- D4: Use 4-bit PTQ in initial rollout but schedule QAT in quarter+1. Rationale: immediate cost wins but needs quality guardrails. Status: APPROVED with monitoring thresholds.

Operational recommendations (concrete runbook items)
- Infra: Provision 2x GPU nodes per region (US-EAST/EU-WEST) with controlled capacity headroom (30% reserve). Node image must include kernel profiles pinned to tested CUDA runtime. Owner: SRE (Jordan Kim). Time: provision within 10 business days after PO.
- Observability: Enable token-level traces, per-route metrics, and retain traces 90 days. Create dashboards for p50/p95/p99, billing per-route, and routing fallback counts. Owner: Observability (Maya Chen).
- Rollout: 2-stage rollout — canary (5% traffic) for 72 hours, then 25% for 7 days, then 100% if no regression. Include automatic rollback on p95 > 120ms or quality regression > 2% NDCG drop. Owner: Solutions Eng (Ethan Patel).
- Autoscaling: latency-first policy with queueing cap; scale step = +1 GPU on sustained p95 > 90ms for 5 minutes. Owner: Platform Eng (Ravi Narayan).

Cost and contract asks (ballpark)
- One-time onboarding engineering cost estimate: 120 engineer-hours (solutions+SRE+obs) -> approx $35k delivery estimate.
- Monthly infra estimate (dedicated reserved pool, 2 nodes per region): $18k–$22k/mo depending on cloud. Add 10% for hot-key replication storage.
- Suggested contract: 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly checkpoints for QAT and model tuning.

Next steps (concrete action items with owners and dates)
- A1: Draft customer-facing readout deck for execs (1 pager + 3 slides: outcomes, recommended path, ask). Owner: Ethan Patel. Due: 2025-11-14.
- A2: Finance finalize reserved pricing and contract terms. Owner: Veridian procurement & Redwood finance liaison (Sofia Alvarez). Due: 2025-11-21.
- A3: SRE provision dedicated nodes and push tested node image. Owner: Jordan Kim. Due: 2025-11-28.
- A4: Observability enablement & create runbooks + alerting thresholds. Owner: Maya Chen. Due: 2025-11-20.
- A5: Schedule 2-week canary window post-provision; set go/no-go gating criteria for each stage. Owner: Ravi Narayan. Due: 2025-12-05.

Customer asks captured during wrap-up meeting
- Veridian asked for a lower-latency SLA (p95 target 90ms) which will require additional capacity or model-level latency engineering.
- They also requested an evaluation of on-prem deployment for EU-only customers (data residency). We proposed a Private deployment feasibility study (4 weeks) — added to backlog.

Open questions for execs / product leadership
- Q1: Approve 12-month reserved capacity contract vs hybrid (mix reserved + burst). Financial modeling attached in linked artifacts.
- Q2: Prioritize QAT work for the 7B model immediately (impact on roadmap and research resourcing).
- Q3: Decide retention policy and access tiering for token-level traces (cost vs debug value).

Appendix — experiment config snapshot (for reproducibility)
- Model variants: rlf-7b-v2 (baseline), rlf-3b-v1 (fallback).
- Quantization: 4-bit PTQ profile used; QAT not applied during POC.
- Batch policy: continuous, max batch size=16, latency cap 120ms.
- Cache strategy: per-user prefix cache, TTL 24h, hot-key replication (top 1k).
- Test harness: synthetic QPS generator + replayed production traces (window: 7 days).

Notes to self / rough items captured during workshop
- Customer values predictability > raw cost; push that in exec deck.
- Add a short appendix describing the fallback decision graph for product folks.
- Flag: Ensure legal signs off on trace retention for EU customers (GDPR review).

End of ledger.
